lead.t: Lymphoedema is caused by inadequacy of the lymphatic drainage, which leads to the accumulation of protein-rich fluid in the interstitium, with chronic inflammation, fibrosis and adipose deposition.

b: Definition: Accumulation of interstitial fluid from impaired lymphatic drainage → progressive accumulation of protein-rich fluid → fibrosis
Pitting oedema in early stages → progressive accumulation
Protein-rich fluid stimulates fibroblast activity → brawny (non-pitting) induration + peau d'orange skin changes
Chronic fibrosis with subcutaneous fibrous thickening

qs.q: A patient living in an endemic region presents with massive, chronic secondary lymphoedema of the lower extremities characterized by brawny induration and thickening of the skin. Which of the following is the most common worldwide cause of this condition?
qs.e: Filariasis is parasitic obstruction of the lymphatic channels and is the most common worldwide cause of massive secondary lymphoedema. Chronic lymphatic blockage leads to increased hydrostatic pressure, ECM deposition, and brawny skin induration.
